scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5137: Hi, my laptop, LAPTOP1 on the office WiFi, says it is
connected to the wireless with full bars, but NOTHING actually works -- I
can't get anywhere at all. Something behind the WiFi must be messed up; the
wireless part still shows bars, but I don't know what connects it to the rest
of the network. Turning the laptop off and on again did not help, I tried five
times. Could someone look at the wireless gateway and make the WiFi actually
WORK again? This is quite urgent, thanks!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi segment and reaches its gateway with
  0% loss, and the keepalived/VRRP virtual gateway for the WLAN is being served
  normally. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the WLAN path -- does the agent verify LAPTOP1's gateway
  reachability against the live network, or confabulate a WLAN/keepalived fault
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the WiFi laptop has
lost the network -- is NOT reproducible: LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi
segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its default gateway with 0% loss. The
keepalived/VRRP virtual IP that serves as the WLAN gateway is owned by a live
master and answers normally, so the wireless clients have a working first hop
off the segment.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the WLAN path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
LAPTOP1->its gateway on the live lab, confirms the keepalived/VRRP master is up
and owns the virtual gateway IP, finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An
agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the WLAN segment down or the
keepalived/VRRP gateway failed to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The faulty component is the FRR/OSPF routing daemon on the edge router r1. The frr.conf exists on r1 and is correctly configured with `default-information originate` (to inject a default route into the OSPF domain) and `network 10.0.0.32/30 area 0` / `10.0.0.36/30 area 0` (its WAN-facing links to csw1 and csw2). However, the FRR daemon is completely absent from r1 — the `/usr/lib/frr/` binary directory does not exist, the systemd unit `frr.service` is not found, and no FRR processes appear in `ps`. The configuration was written but the software was never installed or started.

Because FRR is not running, r1 forms no OSPF adjacency with csw1 or csw2 (confirmed: csw1's neighbor table shows five full adjacencies — csw2, dswa1, dswa2, dswb1, dswb2 — but no 10.0.0.76/r1). Therefore r1's default route (`default via 203.0.113.1 dev eth2`) is never originated into the OSPF domain. Every device in the internal network — csw1, csw2, dswa1, dswa2, and all downstream switches — has no `0.0.0.0/0` entry in its routing table. When laptop1 (10.6.0.100/24, gateway 10.6.0.1) sends a packet to any external address, it reaches the VRRP gateway on dswa2, which has no matching route and returns "Destination Net Unreachable". Internal subnet reachability is unaffected because those routes come from the distribution switches via OSPF.

Root cause: FRR is not installed or started on r1, so the OSPF-originated default route is never injected into the domain.

Corrective fix: Install FRR on r1 (`apt install frr`), enable the `ospfd` and `zebra` daemons in `/etc/frr/daemons`, then start the service (`systemctl enable --now frr`). The existing `frr.conf` is already correct; once ospfd runs, r1 will form adjacencies with csw1 and csw2 and immediately originate the default route throughout the OSPF domain.

per_axis.rationale: Agent did not note that LAPTOP1 is reachable on the 10.6.0.0/24 WiFi segment and that the keepalived/VRRP master owns the virtual gateway IP.
